bullets.text: 10-year Treasury at 4.92%, flat on the day. This is the single biggest input to your rate.
Published 30-year survey at 7.28%, +17 bp week over week. It is a weekly average and always lags your rate sheet.
Mortgage spread 224 bp, normal at the 61th percentile of 10 years. That is 2.24 points of the 7.28% rate coming from spread, not from Treasuries.
30Y Fixed Mortgage Rate +17 bp, bigger than 91% of moves on record. Expect rate sheets to follow.
Core CPI +0.30% (2026-10 reference month), the newest inflation read the market has.

why.headline: Mortgage rates are under upward pressure. The 10-year Treasury is 4.92% (+0 bp on the day) and the modeled 30-year sits near 7.17%.
why.summary: The 10-year Treasury is at 4.92%, +0 bp on the day. Mortgage rates take their direction from the 10-year first. Between the last two published mortgage surveys the 30-year moved +17 bp. That breaks down exactly: -6 bp from Treasuries and +23 bp from the mortgage spread. The mortgage/10-year spread is 224 bp, which is normal and sits at the 61th percentile of the last 10 years. The long-run average is 208 bp, so roughly 16 bp of the current mortgage rate is spread rather than Treasury yield. Intraday spread movement is not observable here. Without a live MBS feed the daily read assumes the spread held and moves the rate with the 10-year only.

contributions.chain: Payrolls → ↓ Recession risk → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Recession fear is the classic bid for duration. Yields fall.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

brief.title: MORTGAGE MARKET MORNING BRIEF
brief.body: Mortgage rates: 7.28% published 2026-11-19, modeled 7.17% today. 10-year Treasury: 4.92% (+0 bp). MBS: 0.00 ticks. Rate bias: Worsening. The mortgage spread is 224 bp, normal versus its 208 bp long-run average. Ahead: Core PCE Price Index on 11-28. Biggest risk: Core PCE Price Index. A hot print reverses any Treasury rally. What LOs should know: protect anything closing inside 30 days and expect reprice risk intraday
